parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
on can mean over, on top of
rigid means strict, unbending

explanation.surface: A fielder takes a catch and grips the ball in a tight, rigid squeeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' and 'over' borrow cricket's vocabulary, but they only supply C and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrict is to make narrower by pressing tightly, a synonym of squeeze.

parts.note: straining, as in going all out, gives out
set means hardened, firm

explanation.surface: Someone strains hard right from the beginning of a task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going all out' is straining your utmost, so 'straining' gives OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An outset is the beginning of something, as in from the outset, a synonym of start.

explanation.surface: A note that something is nourishment for people living in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Swedes are root vegetables eaten as food (rutabaga in America), and Swedes are people from Sweden in northern Europe.

indicators.note: seen only vaguely, the letters of meteor are blurred into a new order

explanation.surface: A meteor glimpsed faintly far off in the night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote means situated far away, synonym of far-distant.

parts.note: to con is to cheat or swindle
done is slang for cheated, as in I've been done

explanation.surface: Forgiving a cheat who has cheated in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone is to overlook or excuse a wrong, a synonym of making allowances for it.

clue.text: He'll effect some simple improvement naturally

definitions.text: He'll effect some simple improvement naturally

parts.words: He'll effect some simple improvement naturally
parts.note: simples are old medicines made from a single plant, so the person who heals with them brings about natural improvement in health

explanation.surface: A man who makes modest, easy improvements without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simple' reads as 'easy', but a simple is a medicinal plant or the remedy made from one.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbalist treats illness with plant remedies, once called simples, healing by natural means.

clue.text: Not worn but in wear-due for replacement

indicators.note: letters up for replacement are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, without the hyphen

explanation.surface: Clothes not yet worn, though they are due a replacement from wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for replacement' shuffles IN WEARDUE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwearied means not tired or worn out, so not worn in the sense of fatigued.

parts.note: pro is short for professional
tracts are long treatises or disquisitions

explanation.surface: A professional reading lengthy treatises keeps at it for hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' is part of the surface picture and acts only as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To protract is to prolong or draw out, keeping something going longer.

clue.text: People enveloping a sovereign's letters appear less public-spirited

indicators.note: the people word wraps round the letter a, so enveloping marks a container

parts.note: men means people
ER, Elizabeth Regina, are the queen's initials seen on post boxes

explanation.surface: People who seal royal mail in envelopes seem rather mean-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' sounds like post, but the sovereign's letters are the royal cipher ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaner means more stingy and selfish, so less generous towards the community.

indicators.note: the word emigrants is rearranged as if its letters were found new accommodation

explanation.surface: A flood of emigrants pouring into their new housing.
explanation.definitionFit: Streaming means flowing or running, as water or a crowd does.

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to start a debate.
explanation.definitionFit: An object is a goal or purpose; to object is to protest or raise an argument against something.

clue.text: Choosing a piece about the French

indicators.note: the piece word goes round the French article, so about marks a container

parts.note: a section is a piece or part
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Selecting a portion of something concerning the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Selection is the act of picking out, a noun matching choosing used as a noun.

indicators.note: disconcerted means thrown into confusion, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A girl who is not in the least flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disconcerted' rearranges AGIRLO; 'She's' defines a female name, with 'a girl' also serving as fodder in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloria is a woman's given name, so a she is a fair definition.

parts.note: temper means anger, as in losing your temper
scoffed means ate greedily

explanation.surface: Someone held back their rage and then wolfed down a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperate means moderate and self-controlled, synonym of restrained.

clue.text: Hiding in the tall grass, put on clothes and made up

indicators.note: the clothing word is concealed within the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall marsh grass
to dress is to put on clothes

explanation.surface: Someone hid in long grass, got dressed and applied make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up' looks like cosmetics but means made amends.
explanation.definitionFit: Redressed means set right or compensated for, as in made up for a wrong.

clue.text: Exceptionally clear note written to show open-mindedness

indicators.note: done exceptionally, outside the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unusually plain note written to display a broad mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is acceptance of views different from your own, synonym of open-mindedness.

explanation.surface: Mix someone a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To peg is to fix in place with pins; a peg is a measure of spirits, especially whisky.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Stuff turning up, get by' (3) for PEN: no parse gives PEN from these words, so the OCR text looks garbled and no source gives the printed clue.

explanation.surface: A snare that was nevertheless brought out.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a snare for catching game; gin is a spirit distilled in a still.

parts.note: the viewer is the eye itself, and its seating is the socket it sits in, not a chair for an audience

explanation.surface: Chairs laid out for a spectator.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyehole is the socket in the skull that houses the organ of sight.

indicators.note: the soft letter goes in the heart of the six-legged creature

parts.note: an insect has six legs, so is a six-footer
P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: A kindly very tall person is running a search party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person; it is an insect with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine closely, a synonym of search.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Rushed in one after another' (3) for NAN: no parse gives NAN from these words, so the OCR text looks garbled and no source gives the printed clue.

clue.text: One who loves being unhappily married!

indicators.note: unhappily signals the letters of married are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A rueful remark that someone who loves ends up miserably wed.
explanation.definitionFit: An admirer is someone who is fond of or courts another.

clue.text: The carrier left with evident hesitation

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: The delivery person left, clearly hesitating.
explanation.definitionFit: A porter carries luggage for travellers.

clue.text: The person scared of company-drawback, that

indicators.note: back after draw means that word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone frightened of the downside of company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawback' looks like one word meaning snag; it splits into DRAW read back, WARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A coward is someone easily frightened, lacking courage.

clue.text: Articles on heartless Norma, once regarded as divine

parts.note: a and the are the indefinite and definite articles

indicators.note: heartless means the middle of Norma is removed, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Writings about a cold-hearted woman once thought godlike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norma' is also a Bellini opera heroine; here it just loses its middle letters ORM.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena was the Greek goddess of wisdom, worshipped as divine in ancient times.

parts.note: in means fashionable or modish
here means present, as in a roll call

explanation.surface: A walking stick handed over as a fashionable gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' and 'present' look like nouns, a cane and a gift; here they are a verb and an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhere is to be fixed in or belong intrinsically, so to stick in something.

clue.text: The consequence to a social worker is grave

parts.note: import means consequence or significance
an ant is a worker in a social insect colony

explanation.surface: A serious result for someone working in social services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' sounds like a caseworker; it is an ant, a worker in an insect colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Important means serious or weighty, synonym of grave.

clue.text: He's a villain, painters state shortly

parts.note: RAs are Royal Academicians, painters
Cal is short for California, a US state

explanation.surface: A bad lot, according to a brief statement from artists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state shortly' reads as speak briefly, but means an abbreviated US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a rogue or scoundrel, a mild word for a villain.

clue.text: Cooks never bake-there's nothing to gain from it

definitions.text: there's nothing to gain from it

indicators.note: cooks as a verb means fiddles or rearranges, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Cooks who never bake find no profit in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooks' looks like the subject; it is a verb meaning tampers with.
explanation.definitionFit: To break even is to finish with neither profit nor loss.

clue.text: Fish without the right, so get cut

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the fish surrounds the right letter

parts.note: a tench is a freshwater fish
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A fish lacking rights gets chopped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like a deletion, but in its old sense means outside, so TENCH goes round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow ditch, a cut dug into the ground.

clue.text: Sorts out those with special qualifications

explanation.surface: Someone arranges the people who hold degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: To graduate is to grade or arrange in steps; graduates are people who hold university degrees.
